round_history.name: r10_through_hole_compound_np_synthesis
round_history.description: Added cardinal+`through hole(s)` compound-NP post-extension at the _DEFINITE_REF consumer site in claims.py. _NP_CORE truncates at `through` because it's listed as a preposition in _STOP_WORDS — but `through hole` is a patent compound noun (a hole that passes through a substrate; MPEP § 2173 element-naming convention). When the captured term is exactly a bare cardinal (two / three / ...) AND the source-text continuation is `through hole(s)`, restore the compound. Tightly gated: cardinal-only prevents over-extension in verb-prep contexts like `the X mounted through holes in the wall`. Cross-jurisdiction parity: CN/TW don't have the same compound-NP truncation pattern (CJK `通孔` is a single token); deferred per DR-1. 0 active corpus labels silenced (mechanism added per real user signal — issue #178 finding 1).

round_history.name: r14_predicative_adj_intro
round_history.description: Reconcile + ship the US predicative-adjective intro-coverage class (PR #296, missed_introduction family). utils.py `_POST_NOMINAL_PREDICATIVE_ADJ` = {indicative, operable, responsive} wired into `_should_strip_trailing` via `_is_trailing_predicative_adj`: the §112(a)/(b) intro extractor over-captured a post-nominal predicative adjective (`a first signal indicative of X` -> intro term `first signal indicative`), so `the first signal` failed to match its own introduction -> antecedent FP. Stripping the predicative adj restores the match. Validated on the corpus FN-guard: -82 walker_fp silenced, silenced_legit=0, protect_violations=0, 1811 tests pass. First attempt used 12 adjectives and the FN-guard caught it silencing 8 real legit findings -> narrowed to the 3 safe ones (DR-1). Labels reconcile: 107 unresolved_removed -> resolved_by r14 (76 walker_fp + 30 unclassified + 1 legit_drafting_error reclassified walker_fp as a verified gold-correction: 'a persistent cache flush handler' intro present in US11868265B2 c1, prior over-capture of trailing 'responsive' masked it; matches phase2b_results_us_corrections.json, attorney-over-corpus/DR-10). 5 shifted clean shapes (`the ... indicative` -> `the neural network using historical data` / `the data` / `the feedback`) dual-labeled per ADR-111 — pre-existing intro-coverage FPs unmasked, not introduced, by r14. Cross-jurisdiction: EPC reuses the US walker (covered for free); CN/TW use different intro extractors (cn_claims.py / tw_claims.py) and CJK has no post-nominal predicative-adjective shape, so no analogue to mirror — deferred per DR-1, no CN/TW report.

round_history.name: r15_inclaim_dep_resolution
round_history.description: US dependency-parser robustness fix (ADR-159 Zero-FP Sweep 1A, antecedent). parser/claims.py `_OFCLAIM_FIX` widened from `(of|to)` to `(of|to|in)`: the US round-1 corpus has 543 `inclaim N` whitespace-collapse artifacts (`as claimed in claim N` / `as recited in claim N` / `as defined in claim N` -> `claimed inclaim N`). `\bclaims?` needs a word boundary before `claim`, which `inclaim` lacks, so `_DEP_REF` missed them -> those dep-claims classified INDEPENDENT -> ancestor chain empty -> every body reference emitted as a spurious 112(b) finding (US9158628B2 alone: ~100). Same PDF/HTML whitespace-collapse root cause as the shipped `of`/`to` normalization (R35) and the documented R11 `as inclaim 1` dep break. Maximally FN-safe: resolving a dependency only ADDS ancestor-intro coverage -> can only SILENCE antecedent FPs, never hide a real missing antecedent. Corpus FN-guard: -1006 walker_fp silenced (985 + 21 ensemble-mislabels reclassified), silenced_legit=0, protect_violations=0, 1811 tests pass. The 21 silenced findings the ensemble had labeled legit_drafting_error were all biased by the SAME broken chain (judged as independent claims with no ancestor); the new fix-shape-aware gold-corrector deterministically confirmed each FN-safe (Pattern-A intro present / term introduced in ancestor / parse-artifact shift) and they are recorded in phase2b_results_us_corrections.json. `\bin` cannot match inside within/main/obtain/begin/protein. Cross-jurisdiction: EPC reuses the US walker (covered for free); CN/TW use their own dep parsers (cn_claims.py / tw_claims.py) and the analogous CJK 引用記載型式 collapse is a SEPARATE sweep item (Sweep 1B/1C) — no US-side action; DR-1 until a CN/TW run surfaces it.

round_history.name: r17_abbrev_plural_with_as_dep
round_history.description: Two FN-safe additive/structural fixes (ADR-159 Zero-FP Sweep 1A-cont, antecedent). (1) utils.py `_ABBREVIATION_PATTERN` now accepts a trailing plural `s` in the parenthetical acronym `([A-Z]{2,}s?)` so pluralized abbreviations `(OIDs)`/`(CSSDs)` register as intros and `the oids` resolves — purely additive intro recognition. (2) parser/claims.py `_OFCLAIM_FIX` widened to `(of|to|in|with|as)`: `in accordance with claim N` (withclaim, 34x) and `media as [claimed in] claim N` (asclaim, 17x) are whitespace-collapsed dependency preambles the same as R15's inclaim — resolving them only ADDS ancestor-intro coverage (FN-safe by construction). Corpus FN-guard: -87 (84 walker_fp + 3 coverage), silenced_legit=0, protect_violations=0. EPC reuses the US walker; CN/TW have their own dep parsers + no parenthetical-acronym FP report — DR-1.

round_history.name: r33_finite_verb_and_participle_stops
round_history.description: Reports #362/#363 (scans/monitors), #374 (include), #375 (built). Four never-noun or noun-gray verb forms over-captured into the antecedent term. (a) 'include' added to _STOP_WORDS: the base form for a plural subject ran the NP capture through the verb into its object ('the reaction condition data include feed temperature'); the 3sg 'includes' was already a stop, the base form was the gap. _STOP_WORDS is the only INTERIOR cut the US capture has - the trailing cleaner cannot reach a verb that has an object behind it. (b) 'enters'/'re-enters'/'built' added to _VERB_STOPS (trailing): no noun sense exists ('entry'/'entrance'; 'built' is an irregular past participle and so is invisible to the -ed heuristic in _is_likely_past_participle - that was the gap). 'built' is deliberately a TRAILING stop and NOT a _STOP_WORDS entry, because the hyphenated modifier 'built-in' is a single _WORD token there and a _STOP_WORDS entry would terminate 'the built-in memory' at 'built' (a real FN). (c) 'scans'/'monitors' added to _CONTEXTUAL_VERB_STOPS gated on a following object determiner (a|an|the) - both are genuinely noun-gray ('the CT scans', 'the display monitors'), so a bare stop would be FN-unsafe; the plural-noun reading is followed by a predicate, never by a determiner. Same gate shape as R32 drive/swing. 'using' was TRIALED AND WITHHELD (reports #357/#364): it silenced 2 gold-legit defects ('the resection using dynamic visualization data' US11896442B2 c16; 'the language model using textual data' US20220309089A1 c7) that are structurally identical to the reported FP ('the <head> using <NP>'), so no surface gate separates them - the cut exposes an intro-side gap it had been masking. Deferred rather than ship an FN. US-only (English-verb over-capture; no CN/TW report, DR-1). Shared _NP_CORE covers spec-support (cross-CHECK); EPC reuses the US walker. GATES: validate_fix silenced_walker_fp=45 / silenced_legit=0 (PASS); examiner FN-guard 0/3173 examiner-confirmed defect terms touched; fixture protect_violations=0; pytest 2856 pass. MPEP 2173.05(e) / 35 USC 112(b). round 32->33.

round_history.name: r34_gated_finite_verbs_trailing_adverb_partitive_pronoun
round_history.description: Reports #391 (sandwich), #397 (closely join), #400 (switched one). Three reference-side over-capture mechanisms, all measured FN-safe. (a) 'sandwich'/'join' added to _CONTEXTUAL_VERB_STOPS gated on a following object determiner (a|an|the) - same gate shape as R32 drive/swing and R33 scans/monitors. Both are noun-gray ('a die sandwich' is a real stacked structure; 'the join operation'/'the join between two tables' in software claims), so a bare _VERB_STOPS entry would be FN-unsafe; the noun reading is always followed by a predicate, never a bare determiner. (b) NEW _TRAILING_ADVERB_STOPS + strip_trailing_adverb: once the finite verb is stripped, the manner adverb modifying it is left stranded in the trailing position ('the ports closely join the other ...' -> 'ports closely' -> 'ports'). A blanket -ly suffix test is NOT safe (assembly/supply/poly/anomaly are real patent nouns), so the set is an explicit curated list of manner adverbs. REFERENCE-SIDE ONLY (never in clean_noun_phrase), following the WS-A3 precedent: an intro-side strip could generalize an introduction and mask a real defect. (c) NEW _is_partitive_pronoun_head: 'the switched one of the plurality of channels' heads on the PRONOUN 'one', not an element - the element is what follows 'of' and is checked by its own reference. Deliberately NARROW because the examiner corpus carries 4 confirmed 112(b) rejections ending in a singular 'one' (the respective one / the at least one / the current one / the first one), all ordinal/quantifier/deictic modifiers: the guard fires only for plural 'ones' or a singular 'one' modified by a PAST PARTICIPLE, which is disjoint from all four (0/3173 reachable). round_history.name: r40_matrix_verbs_and_bare_dependency_preamble

(1) _STOP_WORDS additions, split by noun-grayness per the standing rule that a noun-gray token gets a gate and never a bare stop: bare stops `parses` / `emits` / `lose` (no noun sense in patent diction - the nouns are parser/emission/loss; `lose` must be bare because the reported object `connection` carries no determiner); determiner-gated `reviews` (noun-gray: the peer reviews); coordination-gated `adds` (the R30 charges(?=or) shape); and `fail`, gated exactly like the 3sg `fails` already above it. (2) parser/claims.py: claim-word-less dependency preamble (`The game information system according to 1, wherein ...`). _DEP_REF requires the literal `claim`, so the claim parsed INDEPENDENT, its ancestor chain came back empty, and all five elements introduced in claim 1 re-emitted as spurious §112(b) findings whose own did-you-mean named the identical term - that did_you_mean == term signature is the tell for a broken dependency link rather than an over-capture. The class is not drafter-specific: it independently fires on granted US4763545A c17 (`An automatic transmission as claimed in 14`), where it retires 3 cascade findings. round_history.name: r46_connectorless_dependency_preamble
round_history.description: US R46 - the CONNECTOR-LESS dependency preamble (reports #603/#604/#605/#606/#607/#608). A drafter wrote `The command message exchanging method claim 10, further comprising ...`, dropping `according to`. _DEP_PREAMBLE required one of of/according to/as in/as claimed in/as recited in/as set forth in before `claim N`, so it did NOT match, the dependency preamble was NOT excluded from the body-reference scan, and the walker emitted the reference `the command message exchanging method claim 10` - a string that appears NOWHERE in the draft. SIX reports (five antecedentBasis plus one specSupport) trace to this ONE unexcluded preamble, on a single drafter's claim set. Only the preamble EXCLUSION failed, which is why did_you_mean names the clean head (`command message exchanging method`) instead of being identical to the term. The reading is not newly invented either: _DEP_REF had already committed the claim to depending on 10, so this aligns the exclusion with a dependency the parser had already resolved. The drafter's omission stays visible through the dependency-format check and the claim text is never rewritten. Corpus-silent BY MEASUREMENT, not by luck: all 14 `claim <N>` occurrences in the US corpus are `as claimed in claim N` and ZERO are connector-less, so validate_fix is a clean no-op (0 silenced / 0 false-fires). AUTHORITATIVE examiner FN-guard run FOR REAL because this change SILENCES a scan region - the direction the static substitute is structurally blind to (US R41 lost 3 examiner rejections that way): 1347 -> 1347, LOST 0. round_history.name: r47_positional_superlative_tail
round_history.description: US R47 (report #683 finding [1]) - POSITIONAL SUPERLATIVE tail, mirror of the R41 `-ward` positional gate. The trailing-strip cascade already handled `<noun> located <adverb>` (`located` is a past participle, `radially` an -ly adverb, both strip), but the cascade walks from the END and the first word it met was `outermost` - one unhandled token blocks every strip behind it, so the intro registered as `edge band region located radially outermost` and the drafter's own `the edge band region` no longer matched. `-most` is a CLOSED morphological class of positional superlatives with no noun members in English, and the gate is POSITIONAL exactly as `-ward` is: attributive use (`the topmost conductive coil`) is followed by its head noun so the trailing walk never reaches it. MEASURED on the US corpus: 41 `-most` occurrences, ALL 41 attributive, and ZERO intro captures ending in a `-most` word - so it measures as a corpus no-op and its whole value is the reported end-to-end fix. Gates: validate_fix 10746 -> 10746 (0 silenced_legit, 0 false-fires), UNPAIRED-NEW 0, and the REAL EdgeXpert examiner FN-guard 1347 -> 1347 LOST 0 (never the static substitute, per the R41/R43 standing rule). `-est` superlatives deliberately EXCLUDED: no report (DR-1) and the suffix collides with real nouns (crest/chest/forest/request/interest/harvest). WITHHELD WITH ITS NUMBER - report #683 finding [2], the cataphoric-list introduction: completing R38 so `the following operations:` REGISTERS `operations`/`operation` as introduced silenced 17 gold-legit findings on US20190318433A1 (`the step`/`the steps`, claims 2-18), because that drafter writes `the following steps of:` and then adds BRAND-NEW steps with a definite article. The obvious content-word narrowing was measured too and still silences ~10 of the 17, since the drafter reuses claim 1's content words - there is no surface discriminator between `the step of <a recited step>` and `the step of <a new step>`, so it is withheld, not shipped.

round_history.name: r48_basis_must_precede_reference
round_history.description: US R48 (report #677, a reporter-flagged FALSE NEGATIVE) - antecedent basis must PRECEDE the reference. Introductions were pooled per claim with no notion of position, so an introduction appearing LATER in the same claim satisfied an EARLIER definite reference: claim 9's own `a volume of the first chamber` resolved its earlier `the volume of the tuning channel`, though claim 1 never recites a volume. Wrong under MPEP 2173.05(e). Isolated by ELIMINATION, not assumed: deleting sibling claim 8 changed nothing, and removing only the later intro made the finding appear - the sibling was never the cause. US-only this round; no CN/TW report and the CJK walkers pool intros differently, so DR-1 applies and the mirror is deferred rather than ported blind. SCOPE, narrow because vetoing a basis ADDS findings: ancestor-supplied basis is positionally unconditional and never vetoed; only PATTERN A intros carry trustworthy offsets (new `pattern_a_intro_offsets`, a line-for-line twin of extract_pattern_a_intros); any term reachable through a no-offset arm (bare-noun list, gerund head, self-definition, abbreviation) is left alone; the dependent-claim PREAMBLE is never vetoed; and a veto still falls through to has_bare_noun_introduction, which has always been positional. TWO EARLIER DESIGNS WERE MEASURED AND DISCARDED BY THE CORPUS, not by inspection: (a) a hand-written determiner regex accepted `an electrolyte salt` as introducing `electrolyte` and missed the `andan`/`anda` PDF whitespace collapse the extractor already repairs; (b) re-running the extractor over the TRUNCATED prefix destroyed `comprising:` list context, adding 1,577 findings of which 228 were on known walker FPs. Both are pinned by regression tests. MEASUREMENT: +93 findings, silenced_legit 0, silenced anything 0. **The AUTHORITATIVE examiner FN-guard GAINED 30 real USPTO examiner-confirmed 112 rejections (1347 -> 1377) and LOST 0** - that is ground truth and it outranks the LLM-ensemble labels. UNPAIRED-NEW necessarily reports FAIL and that gate does not apply here: it asks 'did this fix MANUFACTURE findings?', which is the POINT of an FN fix, so the examiner guard is the governing gate. ONE ensemble walker_fp label regressed (US11868265B2 c1 `the persistent cache flush handler`, referenced at offset 424 and introduced at 1162) - read against the claim it IS a reference-before-introduction, so the label is over-strict in the same way the 32 labels R38 gold-corrected were; recorded rather than silently overridden.

round_history.name: r49_gerund_display_head
round_history.description: US R49 (reports #676/#681/#688 - every one a complaint about the emitted TERM, not the count) - REFERENCE-SIDE DISPLAY cleanup. `clean_noun_phrase` falls back to the RAW capture when every token strips away, so the drafter's whole predicate was shown as the element name: `the monitoring operable to predict ...` surfaced as `monitoring operable` 22x on US8706518B2. New `gerund_display_head` emits the gerund head instead, applied at the EMISSION site in claims.py ONLY - resolution, the `seen` dedup, the document dedup key and the ancestor diagnostic all keep the RAW term, so the finding COUNT is provably unchanged (10839 -> 10839, 0 claims changing count, 0 unpaired-new, 67 pure renames). BOTH emitted fields are cleaned because every reporter-facing surface renders `reference_form || term`, so cleaning `term` alone would have been invisible in the UI, the report payload and the PDF. THREE WIDER DESIGNS WERE IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED FIRST, AND ALL THREE WERE WRONG: (a) cleaning the term used for RESOLUTION silenced 3 gold-legit findings (US10977324B2 c2/c13/c18 - the cleaned head `comparing` matches the claim's own `comparing ...` step intro); (b) re-running clean_noun_phrase over its own output is NOT idempotent - its pre-loop 1-2 char variable-identifier strip then destroys REAL element names (`remote ue`->`remote` 9x, `wlan ap`->`wlan` 4x, `relay ue`->`relay` 4x); (c) trusting 'the strip loop consumed everything' as the signal LOST a real USPTO examiner 112 rejection (app 18613510, `the moving speed`) because _should_strip_trailing('speed') is True - the examiner FN-guard is what caught it. The shipped gate is POSITIVE, not residual: the head must be the gerund the intro side rejects and EVERY following token must be a known post-modifier, so noun heads like `speed`/`unit`/`adhesive` keep the drafter's words. Engine-1 US term-quality pin 28 -> 6; the 6 survivors are bare `respective` captures, a leading-adjective shape with no noun in the term at all, which needs the capture widened and is its own round. Examiner FN-guard 1377 -> 1377, LOST 0. 67 labels re-keyed (term/reference_form only, verdicts untouched) so the fixture harness returns to its exact prior baseline.

round_history.name: r50_bare_distributive_selector
round_history.description: US R50 - a bare DISTRIBUTIVE SELECTOR is not an element reference. `a sealing apparatus around the respective said intake and said exhaust ports` and `a third information element from the respective at least one of the original source and the potential relay device` both capture the single word `respective`, because the noun scan stops at the determiner that follows. `the` attaches to the noun phrase, not to the selector, so the selector can never carry an antecedent of its own. NO DEFECT IS LOST: all 6 corpus occurrences sit in a claim where the walker separately flags the real head (`intake` / `relay`), which is why this drops a truncation artifact rather than a finding. ATTORNEY READ (Christopher, 2026-09-02) unblocked it: the ensemble had labelled the IDENTICAL construction both ways - walker_fp on US11492933B2 c8/c11/c12 and legit_drafting_error on US11522827B2 c5/c15/c18 - and the legit rationale contradicts itself, conceding `respective` is an enumerator/selector and then faulting it for lacking an independent antecedent introduction. Attorney-over-corpus applies; 3 gold corrections recorded in phase2b_results_us_corrections.json. Gated on a FOLLOWING DETERMINER so it fires only where the head demonstrably continues past the capture. Reuses the closed `_PREDICATIVE_ADJECTIVES` set factored out of `_DISPLAY_POST_MODIFIERS` in R49, so this is not a new one-member denylist. Engine-1 US term-quality pin 6 -> 0.

round_history.name: r51_trailing_overcaptures
round_history.description: US R51 - four trailing over-capture classes from the 2026-09-03 report batch, each shaped by what the CORPUS says about the token rather than its part of speech in the abstract. (1) `decays` / `elapses` ship as UNCONDITIONAL `_VERB_STOPS` (reports #694/#695 antecedent, #697/#699/#704 spec-support): both measure ZERO determiner-preceded occurrences across 1,200 drafts, and unconditional is REQUIRED because Engine 2 reaches the phrase through `extract_noun_phrases`, which has no following-text argument - a contextual entry could not have fixed the spec-support class the reporters filed. (2) `drives` ships GATED on an object determiner (report #695), because it IS noun-gray: 24 determiner-preceded corpus occurrences (disk drives, belt drives) against 0 for the pair above. Same gate as R32's base form `drive`. (3) A trailing MEASUREMENT CONDITION (`the glass fiber material under 10 GHz`, reports #705/#706), reference-side only, gated on a NUMERAL after the preposition - which is what keeps it off `the device under test`. (4) Trailing `not` (report #693) is DISPLAY-ONLY. Shipping it as an ordinary trailing stop was MEASURED FIRST and silenced 6 gold-legit findings, because the shortened term then resolves; 4 of the 6 are arguably over-strict gold, but 2 (`strand not`, US11072816B2, where claim 1 recites `only one strand` / `the unattached strand`) sit in a genuine MPEP 2173.05(e) gray zone. Silencing on a gray-zone reading is not a call for a strip list, and the report was about the TERM, so only the term changes. WITHHELD WITH ITS NUMBER: `ends`, which has 50 determiner-preceded corpus occurrences, 40 followed by `of` - the plural noun `the ends of the shaft`. The verb reading is distinguished only by a following clause boundary, which noun lists also produce, so there is no gate. Gates: 36 silenced / 30 paired shifts / 6 genuine silences (4 gold walker_fp, 2 unjudged); silenced_legit 6 MINUS 6 paired shifts = 0; UNPAIRED-NEW 0; EXAMINER FN-GUARD 1377 -> 1380, GAINED 3 real examiner-confirmed 112 rejections, LOST 0 - the cleaner terms now match examiner terms. Engine-1 quality US 0; Engine-2 US 189/0 unchanged. 30 labels re-keyed, so the US fixture harness returns to its exact prior baseline.

round_history.name: r52_ed_is_a_suffix_only_when_it_strips
round_history.description: US R52 (reports #716/#717/#718) - `-ed` IS A SUFFIX ONLY WHEN IT STRIPS. `the rotational speed of the motor` was emitted as the bare adjective `rotational`, because `_is_likely_past_participle` was a pure LENGTH heuristic (`len >= 5`) and `speed` ends in `ed`. The same rule cost a real USPTO examiner rejection the same day (`the moving speed`, app 18613510), and `moving speed` had only survived BY ACCIDENT - stripping it emptied the phrase and hit the raw-capture fallback, while `rotational speed` did not. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS MORPHOLOGICAL, NOT A WORD LIST: a real participle has a verb stem once `-ed` comes off (`received` -> `receiv`), while in `speed` the `ed` is not a suffix and the Snowball stemmer (already a dependency, used by check_spec_support) leaves it whole. Measured 17/17 both ways on a control set, and across 1,500 corpus drafts it newly protects exactly FOUR distinct words - `speed` (307 occurrences) plus three base-form verbs (`exceed`/`proceed`/`freed`) pulled into `_ED_STEM_VERBS`. `_ED_NOUNS` stays as an explicit override but no longer has to carry the class one member at a time. SECOND HALF, found by the gate: a protected noun must not SHIELD the verb behind it. Once `speed` stopped stripping, the loop halted there and emitted `second planetary gear set reduces speed` - the R47 one-unhandled-token shape arriving THROUGH a fix. Cut the pair only behind a 3sg FINITE verb, because `moving` is strippable too and `moving speed` is the examiner-confirmed element. THE INTRO-SIDE CONTEXTUAL STOP WAS TRIED IN THE SAME ROUND AND REVERTED WITH ITS NUMBER (reports #714/#715, still open): applying `strip_contextual_verb` to `extract_introductions` fixes the `main control command signal output` intro end to end, but it manufactured 22 findings, because it cleans the INTRO of a pair whose REFERENCE over-captures identically - the R29 desynchronization failure. A matched pair must be cleaned on both sides or neither. Gates: 2 silenced (both PAIRED and both IMPROVEMENTS - `constant` -> `constant speed`), silenced_legit 1 MINUS 1 paired = 0; UNPAIRED-NEW 2, and both were READ and taken to Christopher: `the engine speed` where the claim recites `a speed of the engine`, and `the same speed` with no prior recital - ATTORNEY READ: both are REAL 112(b) problems, so this is an FN RECOVERY rather than manufacture. EXAMINER FN-GUARD 1380 -> 1381, GAINED 1, LOST 0 - independent confirmation of the direction. Engine-1 quality US still 0; pytest 3279; US fixture harness back to its exact prior baseline.

round_history.name: r53_contextual_cleaned_intro_tier
round_history.description: US R53 (reports #714/#715) - THE INTRO/REFERENCE SYMMETRY GAP, FIXED A LAYER UP. The reference side has always applied `strip_contextual_verb` right after `clean_noun_phrase`; the intro side never did, so `detect a main control command signal OUTPUT BY an external main control circuit` registered the intro `main control command signal output` and the dependent claim's clean reference matched nothing. The payload's own `did_you_mean` named the over-captured intro. THE IN-PLACE FIX WAS IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED FIRST, ON 2026-09-03, AND MANUFACTURED 22 FINDINGS: adding the call to `extract_introductions` cleans the INTRO of a pair whose REFERENCE over-captures identically, so references that used to match their equally-dirty intro stop matching - the R29 desynchronization failure. A matched pair must be cleaned on BOTH sides or NEITHER. So this ships as the 2026-08-17 'the fix belongs one layer up' shape plus the #509 additive-tier rule: a SEPARATE supplementary index of intros keyed by their contextual-verb-stripped form, built where the following text is available, and consulted ONLY after every existing resolution tier has failed. The RAW intro is untouched, so everything it resolves today keeps resolving, and an additive tier can only SILENCE - it cannot manufacture. UNPAIRED-NEW is therefore 0 BY CONSTRUCTION, and measured 0. Gates: 1 silenced (gold walker_fp `the identifying`, US10929806B2 c6), silenced_legit 0, UNPAIRED-NEW 0, examiner FN-guard 1381 -> 1381 LOST 0. NON-VACUITY (the guard is an exact no-op, so it was proven separately): the supplementary index produces 28 cleaned forms across 14 of 900 drafts. RESIDUAL NOTED: a few indexed forms are themselves weak as introductions (`identifying`, `user providing`, `loan application submission via`). They can only ever silence a reference whose term matches EXACTLY, and silenced_legit measured 0 on this corpus, but if a future round sees a gold-legit silence with a term in that shape, this tier is the first place to look.

round_history.name: r54_clamps_object_determiner_gate
round_history.description: US R54 (report #746) - `clamps` as a 3sg finite verb, gated on a following OBJECT DETERMINER, joining scans / monitors / drives in _CONTEXTUAL_VERB_STOPS. WHY IT IS NOT A SUFFIX ENTRY: `_is_likely_third_person_verb` clears its 6-char floor for `clamps` but the ending is `-mps`, and that suffix is dominated by NOUNS in patent prose (pumps, lamps, ramps, stamps). The detector is UNCONDITIONAL, so a `-mps` entry would strip real element heads. This is not a closable coverage gap: English does not distinguish a 3sg verb from a plural noun morphologically, so the R52 stemmer trick has no purchase and the only discriminator is positional. WHERE THE EVIDENCE CAME FROM, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE PART: the WALKER CORPUS CANNOT PRICE THIS AT ALL - `clamps` occurs ZERO times across its 705 US drafts (clamp 58 / clamping 23 / clamped 2). The EXAMINER DUMP can, and it settles the gate 7 FOR 7: all three verb readings are followed by `the` (`...plate clamps the clamping slot`, `...shell that clamps the rotating plastic column`, `...configured to clamp clamps the radiator`) and all four noun readings by `or` (`clips, clamps or magnets`; `rail clamps or ESD diodes` x3). Not one noun reading carries a determiner, so the gate is DISJOINT from every measured FN. When the walker corpus is silent on a token, the examiner corpus is the second instrument to reach for before withholding. Gates: EXAMINER FN-GUARD (the REAL one, EdgeXpert direct, 1,837 apps) 1381 -> 1381, LOST 0. The no-op is proven NON-VACUOUS separately: the gate fires on exactly 3 of the 7 examiner `clamps` sites and leaves the other 4 untouched. US corpus unchanged by construction (0 occurrences). Cross-jurisdiction: EPC reuses the US walker via utils.py, so it inherits this for free; no CJK analogue (this is an English inflection class).

round_history.name: r55_irregular_past_participles
round_history.description: US R55 (report #762) - THE ENGLISH IRREGULAR PAST-PARTICIPLE PARADIGM. `_is_likely_past_participle` keys on the `-ed` SUFFIX, so every irregular form was invisible to it and `the pushing rod driven by the actuator` kept the participle in the term. These are COMMON, not exotic: across 705 US drafts given 175, driven 71, written 50, taken 22, known 18, shown 15. IT IS A CLOSED MORPHOLOGICAL CLASS, NOT A GROWING DENYLIST - English has a finite irregular paradigm, and listing it is the same move R52 made when it replaced a length heuristic with the stemmer, applied to the words the stemmer cannot reach because their suffix is not -ed at all. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: set / put / cut / hit / read - the participle is identical to the base form AND to a common noun (`the offset set`, `the data read`), so a trailing strip cannot separate them. R43 BISECT, 17 members measured individually against a 10,828-finding baseline. WITHHELD WITH THEIR NUMBERS: `taken` (4 ended, 2 gold-legit silenced) and `shown` (1 ended, 1 silenced). In both the participle heads a REDUCED RELATIVE that is the drafter's real element name - `the action taken`, `the sequence shown` - so stripping it lets the bare noun match an earlier intro and silences a real defect. One of taken's two is TOKEN-ABSENT (`the network path`, containing no participle at all), the spurious-intro cascade signature. `written` is the productive member on its own: 17 FPs ended, 0 legit, 0 unpaired. Gates: 10828 -> 10808, 18 walker_fp silenced, silenced_legit 0, UNPAIRED 0, ZERO new keys at all (a pure silencing, no paired shifts). EXAMINER FN-GUARD (the REAL one, EdgeXpert direct, 1,837 apps) 1381 -> 1381, LOST 0 - and that no-op is proven NON-VACUOUS: the members fire on 880 spans of examiner text (given 201, known 166, driven 159, chosen 86, written 69). Cross-jurisdiction: EPC reuses the US walker via utils.py and inherits it; no CJK analogue.

round_history.name: r56_object_and_adverb_tails
round_history.description: US R56 (reports #761, #780, #762 [2], #781, #783) - THREE OVER-CAPTURE TAILS, each gated on a discriminator the drafter's own text supplies. (1) A NUMERIC COMPARATIVE on an INTRODUCTION (#761/#780): `a first tilt angle less than 45 degrees` registered `first tilt angle less than 45`, so the dependent claim's `the first tilt angle` matched nothing and did_you_mean was null. The intro-side comparative strip has been withheld since WS-A3 because `an inner diameter larger than the inner diameters` then resolved an unrelated reference (US7811436B2 c18), and an in-place intro clean desynchronizes identically dirty pairs (R53). So it goes in the R53 ADDITIVE index, consulted only after every tier fails, and it is gated on a DIGIT after `than` - a comparison against a value, which is exactly what separates it from that FN. (2) `<adverb> <bare verb>` at a REFERENCE tail (#762 [2]/#781): `the second rail radially pass through` captured `second rail radially pass`; `pass` is noun-gray so no strip reached it and the adverb never became trailing. An adverb cannot premodify a head noun, so the word after it at the end of a noun phrase is a predicate. Gated on the curated manner set plus a closed DIRECTIONAL -ly class (perpendicularly/radially/axially/...), never on a bare -ly suffix (`monthly fee`, `family member`). Reference-side only, like R34. (3) A FINITE VERB before a BARE CARDINAL object (#783): `the lid member covers one portion` ran through `covers` because the noun scan halts at an article but not at `one`/`another`/`two` - `covers a portion` never had the bug, so the verb list was not the gap. Cut only at an explicit _VERB_STOPS member (never the 3sg suffix heuristic) and never before `each`/`both`/`all`, which float after a plural subject. Gates: 10808 -> 10798, 10 walker_fp silenced (adverb tail 6, numeric comparative 4), silenced_legit 0, UNPAIRED 0, ZERO new keys. Arm (3) silences nothing on the walker corpus and is proven NON-VACUOUS separately: it fires on 5 corpus spans and 25 examiner spans, every sampled cut correct (`top cover plate covers one electrode` -> `top cover plate`). EXAMINER FN-GUARD (the REAL one, EdgeXpert direct, 1,837 apps) 1381 -> 1383, LOST 0, GAINED 2 - both read and both from arm (2): `second wall portion electrically coupling` -> `second wall portion` and a doubled `... reservoir optically readable` tail, each now matching a real examiner rejection. Spec-support US 189 -> 189 with identical terms; term-quality PASS. Cross-jurisdiction: EPC reuses the US walker via utils.py and inherits all three. TW/CN already ship the verb + CARDINAL interior cut (TW R38 超過一, R35 傳遞一), so arm (3) is the English parity of an existing CJK mechanism; arms (1) and (2) have no CJK analogue (no article system, no -ly morphology).

round_history.name: r57_finite_verbs_and_predicate_tails
round_history.description: US R57 (reports #789, #793, #797, #798, #799, #801, #803-#808) - one class, THREE DRAFTS: the capture ran into the predicate. (1) FINITE VERBS in the shared capture core `_STOP_WORDS`, which feeds BOTH the reference regex and the intro patterns, so a matched pair halts identically and cannot desynchronize (R29/R52): presses, brings, returns, shifts, senses, protrude(s), diffuse. The 3sg suffix heuristic `_is_likely_third_person_verb` could reach none of them (6-char floor plus a suffix list whose own comment defers -rns/-ops), and it cannot be taught to: English does not separate a 3sg verb from a plural noun morphologically (see `clamps`). So each member is gated by its MEASURED profile, contexts READ not totalled: presses/brings/returns verb-only in the corpus but noun-gray in English, gated on the verb complement excluding `of`; shifts NOUN-GRAY in the corpus itself (`distributional shifts of`), gated on a particle or object determiner; senses takes a BARE object (`senses ultraviolet energy`) so it is gated negatively on the noun followers; protrude has no noun sense; diffuse is an ADJECTIVE in every corpus hit and is gated on a following preposition. WITHHELD WITH ITS NUMBER: `drops` (#823) - both corpus uses are nouns (`voltage drops.`) followed by the same punctuation as the reported verb, so no lookahead separates them; pinned by a test. (2) PREDICATIVE `complementary` (#807/#808), positional like the -ward class: attributive use is followed by its head noun, predicative by `to`/`with`. (3) NOMINAL COMPARATIVE in the R53 ADDITIVE index (#803-#805): `a low X lower than the high X` registered `low X lower than`. The US7811436B2 c18 FN that withheld the in-place strip had one shape - the complement named the SAME element - so the arm is gated on the complement's number key differing from the stripped intro's; a test proves the gate load-bearing (gate off silences two real defects). Gates: 10798 -> 10785; silenced 14 (all unjudged, every one read: 10 verb over-captures, 4 `logical storage capacity larger than the sum` genuine intros), silenced_legit 0; UNPAIRED 0 with 1 paired shift (`transmission shifts`/`transmission shifts down` -> `transmission`, matching the same doc's claim 3 at HEAD); honest ended 12. EXAMINER FN-GUARD (real, EdgeXpert direct, 1,837 apps) 1383 -> 1383, LOST 0; non-vacuous: the new stops fire 208x on examiner claims and the comparative shape 1,604x in 462 apps. Spec-support US 189 -> 189, term-quality PASS. CROSS-CHECK: Engine 2 inherits arms (1) and (2) through `_NP_CORE` (verified: `shifting stage shifts down` -> `shifting stage`, which also resolves the FP finding of mixed report #811); arm (3) is antecedent-only by construction, and US spec-support emits 0 `than`-ending terms on its corpus, so no mirror is owed. D1 refnum engine already clean on these shapes. Cross-jurisdiction: EPC reuses the US walker via utils.py and inherits all three; no CJK analogue (no 3sg morphology, no article system).

round_history.name: r58_subordinate_clause_final_verb
round_history.description: US R58 (report #823) - closes the `drops` member R57 WITHHELD, by POSITION rather than by word. `when the bus voltage drops, ...` captured `bus voltage drops`; `drops` is noun-gray (`linear voltage drops.`) and both readings take the same punctuation, so no lookahead separates them. The discriminator is the CLAUSE: a clause opened by a pure subordinator (when / whenever / if / once / unless / while / wherein / whereby) needs a finite verb, so when it ends right after the `-s` word, that word is the verb. before / after / until / as are EXCLUDED because they are also prepositions, where the noun reading is grammatical (`before the voltage drops, ...`). Consumed ONLY as a last-resort resolution tier after R53, and it resolves only when the stem is a registered introduction, so it silences but can never manufacture (the order matters: stripping in the cleaner would turn `when the optical lens, as mounted, rotates` into a non-resolving `optical`). Singular -s nouns (glass, bus, apparatus, axis) excluded. Gates: silenced 6, all read and all correct (`first timer expires`, `timer expires` x2, `second conductive element pivots`, `first power transmission path remains [established]` x2), silenced_legit 0, ZERO new keys, UNPAIRED 0. The two `remains` cases are the R28 withheld shape and stay safe by construction: R28's FN had a stem that is NOT an introduction, which this tier cannot resolve. EXAMINER FN-GUARD (real, EdgeXpert direct, 1,837 apps) 1383 -> 1383, LOST 0. The R57 `drops` pin is kept as a capture-stop withhold (outside a pure subordinate clause, `as the bus voltage drops.`, it still flags). Cross-jurisdiction: EPC inherits via the shared US walker; no CJK analogue (no 3sg morphology). Engine 2 unaffected (resolution-side only).

round_history.name: r59_known_intro_predicate_tail
round_history.description: US R59 - a reference that ran on into a predicate resolves against the drafter's own introduction of its head (reports #823-#959 cluster: drops / returns / only / writes / issues / spans / further cause / communicate / clamp). The 38 US antecedent FP reports were one SIDE: did_you_mean already named the introduced head in nearly every one. Last-resort additive tier after R58, so it can only silence. The head gets the walker's full basis test (ancestor intro, or a same-claim intro BEFORE the reference - an unordered check silenced gold-legit), quantifier heads excluded. The tail decides, measured on gold: unconditional silenced 220 gold-legit (compound nouns: axes / data / frequency); shipped classes = closed adverbs + adverb suffixes, -ing + object, a lone 3sg verb + object or preposition, and a base-form verb only after a plural or coordinated subject (grammar, not a word list). Withheld with numbers: base-form verbs after a singular subject (83 FP / 32 legit before a preposition - they read as compound nouns), multi-word 3sg tails (104 / 10). Result: silenced_walker_fp 231, coverage 2, unjudged 79, silenced_legit 11 read one by one (4 gold errors - head properly introduced; 3 duplicates whose claims stay flagged; participle tails on introduced heads; 1 gray article-less intro), UNPAIRED-NEW 0, real examiner guard LOST 0 / 1,383 recalled. US-only mechanism: CN/TW resolve over-captured tails through their own prefix fallback; no CJK mirror.

round_history.name: r60_distributive_ordinal_and_acronym
round_history.description: US R60 - two additive introduction arms (report #968). (a) An ordinal before an inline acronym: 'a first <expansion> (ABBR) <noun>' also registers 'first abbr noun' (ruling R12, Christopher 2026-10-27: an acronym defined in parentheses at the introduction gives basis to the ordinal plus acronym form); skipped when the expansion itself contains an ordinal (first in first out (FIFO)). (b) Distributive ordinals: 'a first and a second X', 'first and second Xs', 'a first, second, and third X' register every ordinal with the noun of the last; definite runs are references and are skipped; the intros carry offsets so the R48 same-claim ordering rule applies.
